A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, figures, equations, and complete appendices support comparison, including matching retained material across renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original CIFAR and BigGAN image-classification experiments, Gaussian-mixture simulations, and supplementary phase-dynamics results.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds experiments on optimal-FLS scaling and validation-based early stopping.

M1.justification: The output rescaling, learning-rate compensation, balanced initialization, logistic objective, and gradient-flow procedure remain unchanged. The additional CNN is an experimental configuration, while the transfer relation is studied without introducing a new training algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions use CIFAR-10/100, BigGAN-generated dog images with effective dimensions 32, 64, and 128, and Gaussian-mixture classification. Additional generated samples and a validation split retain the same data and task coverage.

E2.justification: The original comparisons retain VGG19 and ResNet18/34/50. The new five-layer CNN scaling study does not add a competing method to those comparisons, and newly cited theoretical works are not evaluated as baselines.

E3.justification: v2 adds CNN width and training-set-size sweeps, with the optimal multiplier selected by minimum test loss. Appendix A.3 adds a fixed validation set comprising 20% of the original training set and stopping at minimum validation loss. The original experimental protocols remain intact.

E4.justification: Section 5.4 newly tests whether the optimal FLS follows predicted scaling across width and sample size. Appendix A.3 checks whether its optimum persists under validation-based stopping. Existing intrinsic-dimension, predictor-norm, and phase-dynamics analyses are retained.

E5.justification: The original heatmaps retain three-seed means and standard deviations. No revised run counts, confidence intervals, or significance procedures are reported; the new experiments do not disclose an additional uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Figure 6 adds optimal-multiplier scaling results. Table 1 adds validation-stopping accuracies, including 73.35% at multiplier 2^-6; its 76.62% peak-accuracy baseline already appears in v1 Figure 9c. These are different stopping settings, not a performance improvement. The redefined g(alpha) curve changes, while the original accuracy heatmaps and other simulation results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Theorem 5.6 and Appendix C.4 replace the complexity-bound argument with fixed enclosing cones, a discretization grid, and Gaussian complexity, changing the bound itself. Proposition 5.7 replaces v1's separate asymptotic limits with a joint-growth analysis, and Proposition E.1 newly supplies conditions for orthogonal separability. v2 also corrects the Gaussian signal convention and strengthens Corollary 5.3 from an upper bound to proportionality despite retaining its proof.

C1.justification: The abstract and introductory contributions retain the same central claims: intermediate FLS can generalize best, excessive feature learning can hurt, and an over-alignment/over-fitting trade-off explains the phenomenon. The rewritten conclusion preserves these claims.

C2.justification: v2 explains over-fitting through enlargement of the hypothesis cone and explicitly distinguishes its upper bound from the exact error component. It adds interpretation of the moderate joint-growth regime and qualifies transfer evidence as limited to simple networks, leaving larger architectures for future work.

D1.justification: Appendices A.1-A.3 document 10,000 additional generated images, the five-layer CNN and channel-width variation, batch size 128 with plain SGD for the transfer study, and validation-set construction. Existing hardware and training disclosures remain, with no new code or data access information.

R1.justification: v2 adds references and local positioning concerning maximal-update parametrization, Gaussian-mixture asymptotics, hyperparameter transfer, and complexity bounds, including Karkada, Mignacco, Refinetti, and Mlodozeniec. The principal contrast with prior extreme-regime FLS analyses remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 locally rewrites the theoretical discussion and conclusion, adds explanatory subsections and acknowledgements, and updates publication and correspondence text. Appendix organization changes around the revised proofs, but the overall narrative and most retained prose remain stable.

P2.justification: v2 adds the cone illustration in Figure 4, scaling plots in Figure 6, and stopping-comparison Table 1. The former Figure 4 becomes Figure 5 with a revised g(alpha) curve and axis. Other figures retain their displays apart from numbering and limited caption edits.

improvement.justification: The stopping check, transfer study, geometric explanation, and explicit separability conditions add useful support and clarity. However, the revised central proof contains an invalid transition from Equations (126) to (127) in Appendix C.4.1, for example at d=3 and r=0.5. Corollary 5.3 also claims proportionality without strengthening its upper-bound proof. These issues make the theoretical gains uncertain, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
